_doc: F1 IDENTICAL-TWIN fail-closed patch — REAL execution proof. Every field below is derived from actual test runs (tests/f1-identity-test.ts pure, tests/f1-identity-browser-test.ts real Chromium), not hand-rolled expectations. No fake PASS: the refusal, mutation count, and final DOM state were read back from the live browser after the act.
invariant: A target is actionable only if its structural fingerprint is UNIQUE within the set a sibling/div reorder could route the selector to. If not unique → refuse (ok:false, reason 'indistinguishable-twin'), mutate neither, record no inverse.

fixture.html:
Article Title

Twin card text

fixture.note: Two genuinely-identical <article class="card"> siblings — same tag, same class, same child structure, same text. A structural fingerprint cannot distinguish them.

initialTarget.howDerived: buildStableSelector (core/inventory.ts) chains the card from the main#main anchor via :nth-of-type(1). Verified real: tests/f1-identity-browser-test.json case 7a returned exactly this selector.

fingerprintValues.note: The browser probe read both cards' tag|class|text directly. They are identical (the twin condition). The full structural fingerprint (identity.ts: tag|attrs|c|d|text(40)|shortHash) is identical for both because text, attrs, childCount, depth are all identical.

duplicateCount.howDerived: stripPositional('main#main > article:nth-of-type(1)') removes :nth-of-type(1). The relaxed selector is the set a sibling reorder could route the original selector to.

reorderOperation.applied: observe card A via describePage (registers identity at selector), then DOM reorder: main.insertBefore(B, A) so B is now first — B occupies the nth-of-type(1) slot the original selector targets.
reorderOperation.afterReorder: card B is at main#main > article:nth-of-type(1); card A is now nth-of-type(2). fingerprint(B) === fingerprint(A) (identical).
reorderOperation.attackWithoutPatch: a bare fingerprint-verify would PASS (B has A's fingerprint) and mutate the WRONG twin (B).

case_twinRefuse.error: target "main#main > article:nth-of-type(1)" is structurally indistinguishable from another element (identical tag, attributes, text, and children). Revueon cannot determine which one you mean, so it refuses to change either. Give the target a stable distinguishing anchor (a unique id, data-testid, role, or aria-label) or target a parent that uniquely contains the one you want, then call describePage and retry.

case_reorderRefuse.expectedFingerprint: fingerprint of card A (observed before reorder)
case_reorderRefuse.afterReorder: card B at the selector slot, fingerprint(B)==fingerprint(A)
case_reorderRefuse.note: The twin check fires on the post-reorder tree regardless of the observe-time fingerprint — identity is genuinely ambiguous, so the act is refused. This is the exact attack the patch prevents.

refusalReason.namesAlternative: stable distinguishing anchor (id/data-testid/role/aria-label) or a parent that uniquely contains it
refusalReason.rule13: the error names an alternative recovery path, not a bare 'target not found'

mutationCount.evidence: tests/f1-identity-browser-test.json case 7g: before=["block","block"] after=["block","block"] — neither twin's computed display changed.
mutationCount.evidenceReorder: case 8d: before=[{display:block,text:'Twin card text'},{display:block,text:'Twin card text'}] after=identical — neither card mutated.

transactionCount.evidence: case 7h: anyHidden=false — no CSS sheet was inserted (hide's CSS would set display:none; neither card is display:none). guardTarget refused before emitAndInsert/recordStructural, so no inverse and no structural entry.
transactionCount.note: The guard runs BEFORE the mutation (act.ts guardTarget short-circuits the tool). On refusal the tool returns g.result before any sendInsertCSS / el.textContent= / insertAdjacentElement / recordStructural call. This is the safety boundary, not a message swap.

finalDomState.twinRefuse: both cards remain <article class="card">Twin card text</article>, display:block, no display:none, no inserted nodes, no data-rv stamps.
finalDomState.reorderRefuse: both cards present, unchanged text, unchanged display. The reorder (B before A) persists; no act reversed or extended it.

distinctSiblingsAct.fixture: <article class="card">First card unique text AAA</article><article class="card">Second card unique text BBB</article>
distinctSiblingsAct.result: ok:true (the named card hidden, the other visible)
distinctSiblingsAct.evidence: case 9b/9c — distinct-text siblings are NOT twins (distinct fingerprints), so legitimate targeting is preserved. The rule does not over-refuse.
distinctSiblingsAct.purpose: acceptance criterion 8: legitimately distinguishable elements still work.

idAnchoredUniqueWithTwinsElsewhere.evidence: pure test 'twin CONTROL: id-anchored unique target' — an id-anchored selector is its own flippable set of size 1, never trips on twins elsewhere.
idAnchoredUniqueWithTwinsElsewhere.purpose: the scope (flippable set) is correct, not whole-document.

existingManyMatch.evidence: pure test 'bare selector matching both → still ambiguous' — the many-match path is unchanged; the twin check runs only on exactly-one-match.
existingManyMatch.purpose: acceptance criterion 7: existing zero/many refusal intact.

existingWrongTarget.evidence: pure test wrong-target cases still pass — the fingerprint compare (now after the twin check) still refuses a re-rendered element whose fingerprint differs.
existingWrongTarget.purpose: no regression to the verified wrong-target path.

scopeDecision.whatIsAStructuralTwin: another element in the set a sibling/div reorder could route the selector to (the 'flippable set' = selector with positional pseudo-classes :nth-of-type/:nth-child/:first|last|only-* stripped) that shares the resolved element's full structural fingerprint.
scopeDecision.whyNotSameParent: a same-parent check would UNDER-refuse: a deeper <div> reorder reroutes an anchored chain's :nth-of-type(k) part (e.g. adding/removing a <section> shifts the count). The relaxed-selector scope catches that deeper reorder.
scopeDecision.whyNotWholeDocument: a whole-document check would OVER-refuse: an id-anchored main#main > article:nth-of-type(1) relaxes to main#main > article, excluding a fingerprint-twin in #footer that the anchored selector could never route to.
scopeDecision.whyRelaxedSelector: it is the one scope that is both sound (catches sibling AND div reorders) and precise (excludes unreachable cross-subtree twins). This resolved the scope question without asking — it is not genuinely ambiguous once the architecture is read.
scopeDecision.noNthOfTypeIndex: no 1-based index, no DOM-order identity, no nth-of-type as persistent identity, no stamped attribute, no UUID — the policy is refuse-when-not-unique, period.

outOfScope.phase5_f4_continuity: NOT touched. No persisted fingerprints, no replay fingerprints, no SPA persistence, no origin/path persistence, no first-paint replay.
outOfScope.parseDeath_wall: NOT touched. No parse retries, no model-JSON reliability, no budget-exhaustion work, no Cloudflare changes.
outOfScope.newDisambiguator: NOT built. No twin index, no coordinate identity, no model-named distinguishing feature. The fix is refuse-only.
outOfScope.otherF1: secondary CSS selector guarding, chain-depth redesign, confidence-model — NOT changed (unless the review found a directly-required one).

honestLimitation: A structural fingerprint CANNOT distinguish two genuinely-identical siblings — that is irreducible. This patch does NOT claim to make them distinguishable; it makes Revueon REFUSE to act when the current identity evidence cannot determine which physical element is intended, rather than guessing (pick-first / trust nth-of-type). The correct claim: when the current identity evidence cannot distinguish the target from an identical twin, Revueon now refuses to act rather than guessing.

undoTwinFix.finding: #1 RUNNER major — the undo verify (applyInverse setText) did a bare querySelector + fingerprint compare with NO twin check. The act itself can CREATE a twin (setText A->'B' makes A and B identical); a reorder reroutes the undo to B (fp(B)==act-fp) -> bare verify PASSES -> clone restores onto the WRONG twin (B corrupted; the mutated A left unrestored).
undoTwinFix.fix: applyInverse (core/ops/txn.ts) now runs the SAME resolveTarget guard via a new DomAdapter.identityDom() accessor — one authoritative identity decision for both the act and undo paths, catching zero/many/wrong-target AND twin. A refused undo throws (counted failed); the clone is NOT applied.
undoTwinFix.proof_pure: tests/f1-identity-test.ts undo-twin case: before='B' after='B' (clone NOT applied; wrong-twin corruption would set after='orig'); refused undo counts failed; the mutated node untouched. Control: distinct (non-twin) siblings undo normally (undone=1, text='orig').
undoTwinFix.scopeRuling: The verifier left this stillBroken. I assessed it as in-scope: the invariant 'a target is actionable only if identity can establish uniqueness' must hold on the undo path too (acceptance criteria 3 & 5), and the spec permits fixes 'directly necessary to make the identical-twin fail-closed invariant actually work.' It reuses the one guard, adds no second system, no persistence, no parse-death work.

resolved.title: undo verify skipped the twin check (act creates a twin, reorder reroutes undo to wrong twin)
resolved.fix: applyInverse uses resolveTarget via DomAdapter.identityDom() — one guard for act+undo

resolved.title: hide healing CSS selectors bypassed guardTarget (reorder reroutes a positional healing selector onto wrong twin via cascade)
resolved.fix: hide parses the full sheet, guards every comma-part via guardTarget, drops any healing rule whose selector refuses (keeps the guarded primary hide)

resolved.fix: regexes now use \(([^)]*)\) to strip every an+b form
